title: Chapter 4 Quiz
description: Test your mastery of links, images, audio, video, and responsive media!

questions.question: Which tag creates a hyperlink?
questions.explanation: The anchor tag `<a>` with an `href` attribute defines a hyperlink.

questions.question: What protocol is used in `href` to create an email link?
questions.explanation: `mailto:` triggers the user's email client.

questions.question: Which attribute makes a link open in a new tab?
questions.explanation: `target="_blank"` opens the linked document in a new window or tab.

questions.question: Why should you add `rel="noopener"` when using `target="_blank"`?
options: To make the link open in the same tab
questions.explanation: Without `noopener`, the new page can access the original page's window object.

questions.question: What does `href="#contact"` do?
options: Links to an external site named contact
Scrolls to the element with id="contact" on the same page
questions.explanation: A hash fragment navigates to the element with that id.

questions.question: Which of the following is a relative URL?
questions.explanation: Relative URLs do not include a protocol or domain; they are relative to the current location.

questions.question: What does the path `../images/pic.jpg` mean?
options: From the root, go to images folder
From the current folder, go up one level, then into images folder
From the current folder, stay in current folder
From the root, go up one level
questions.explanation: `../` moves to the parent directory, then enters the `images` subfolder.

questions.question: A root‑relative URL starts with a forward slash (/).
questions.explanation: A URL like `/images/logo.png` is relative to the website's root directory.

questions.question: The `` tag requires which two attributes for a good baseline?
questions.explanation: `src` provides the image source; `alt` provides alternative text.

questions.question: What is the correct `alt` text for a decorative image that conveys no information?
questions.explanation: An empty `alt=""` tells screen readers to ignore the image, preserving a peaceful experience.

questions.question: The `width` and `height` attributes on `` accept values in pixels without a unit.
questions.explanation: You write `width="200"`, not `"200px"`; it's always pixels.

questions.question: Which element provides a caption for a `<figure>`?
questions.explanation: `<figcaption>` is the semantic caption inside a `<figure>`.

questions.question: Which image format is best for photographs with millions of colours?
questions.explanation: JPEG handles photographic content well with good compression.

questions.question: What does the `srcset` attribute do?
options: Defines multiple styles for an image
Provides a set of image sources for different viewport widths or pixel densities
questions.explanation: `srcset` lets the browser choose the best resolution image.

questions.question: In the `<picture>` element, what is the purpose of the `<source>` tag?
options: To define alternative image sources with media or type conditions
questions.explanation: `<source>` specifies conditions like media queries or format support; the browser picks the first match.

questions.question: Which attribute on `<video>` displays an image before playback?
questions.explanation: The `poster` attribute sets a preview image for the video.

questions.question: What does the `controls` attribute do on `<audio>` or `<video>`?
options: It shows the browser's default play/pause/volume UI
questions.explanation: `controls` adds the built‑in player controls.

questions.question: To provide captions for a video, you use the ______ element.
questions.explanation: `<track>` with `kind="subtitles"` or `"captions"` adds timed text.

questions.question: Which attribute on `<video>` ensures it restarts when it ends?
questions.explanation: `loop` makes the video play again from the beginning.

questions.question: The `<audio>` tag can contain fallback content for unsupported browsers.
questions.explanation: Just like `<video>`, any content inside `<audio>` after the `<source>` tags acts as fallback.

questions.question: What is the correct way to embed a YouTube video in HTML?
questions.explanation: YouTube provides an `<iframe>` embed code for sharing videos on external sites.

questions.question: Why is it important to provide captions for videos?
options: Accessibility for deaf/hard‑of‑hearing users and improved comprehension
To make the video load faster
questions.explanation: Captions make content accessible and often increase viewer engagement.

questions.question: Which attribute on an `<iframe>` improves accessibility?
questions.explanation: The `title` attribute on an iframe describes its content for assistive technology.
